calls.reason: BofA, as reported by Fortune, found hyperscalers could fund capex from about $577B in operating cash flow while debt rose only about $77B, and OpenAI's $110B raise was equity. Oracle is the main exception.

Wood Mackenzie found a 30% power-transformer supply deficit and named electrical steel and labor as constraints, and 92% of firms in the AGC/NCCER 2025 survey had trouble hiring. Thyssenkrupp's European oversupply is only a partial caveat.

Reporting shows OpenAI lost billions and Anthropic projected a loss of about $5B. But no earlier baseline is identified, and the audited revenue (about $13B) roughly matches what was reported, so the 'billions less, spent billions more' part is unverified.
No independent evidence of the $2.66B AWS figure was found; it traces back to Zitron's own reporting. The CFO declaration gives only a lower bound for lifetime compute spend.

EIA shows Brent kept rising to an April 2026 peak. The TAC/Baltic index had air freight about 33% above a year earlier, jet fuel 57% higher, and strong gains on Taiwan-to-US routes, though AI cargo demand added to that.
Rao's declaration gives only lower bounds (over $5B revenue, over $10B spend), and nothing in the packet shows deliberate deception. The intent claim is neither supported nor disproved.
